thesis: Method-test thesis: Kirby is a cyclical, capital-heavy tank-barge operator (28% of the ~4,004-barge US inland fleet, Jones Act protected) plus an engine/power-generation distributor riding data-center backup and prime-power demand; over 5 years it compounds EPS ~4-9%/yr (pricing on a near-fixed fleet plus ~4-5%/yr buybacks) at a return on total capital close to its cost of capital (~10%), so shareholder returns track EPS plus buybacks minus any de-rating from today's ~17x forward P/E.
variant_view: Market (reverse DCF): at $122.89 (19.4x FY25 EPS, 17.0x the FY26 guide, 9.5x EV/EBITDA, FCF yield 6.3%) the worksheet's NOPAT-based DCF cannot reproduce the price at a 10% ROIIC; even at a 20% ROIIC (sensitivity file, written after the outputs) the price needs ~11%/yr revenue growth for 10 years or a 17% NOPAT margin (FY25 11.1%). On reported FCF the price is consistent with ~3.8% perpetual FCF growth at a 9.5% cost of equity, i.e. roughly fair if 2025's cash taxes (bonus depreciation, deferred tax $82M) persist. Our view: NO claimable mispricing, with a mild negative tilt. What the market appears to price: an inland up-cycle (utilization low-90%, term renewals 'north of inflation', newbuilds 60-70/yr only matching retirements) plus a power-generation growth story (backlog > $1.5bn, book-to-bill > 1). What we verified that cuts against it: (1) ROTC 10.4% over 2023-25 (proxy) - the business earns about its cost of capital even at good points of the cycle; (2) contract escalators slowed from +9.5% (Jan-2024) to +3-5% (Jan-2025) and term renewals were flat to low-single-digit in 2025-26 - the rate cycle has been decelerating, not accelerating; (3) 2026 inland margins are capped by fuel ($3.91/gal Q3-26 vs $2.46) with a ~120-day escalator lag, and the Jones Act waiver (17-Mar-2026, now extended to 14-Feb-2027) adds foreign-flag competition risk in coastal; (4) 21 open-market insider sales, 0 buys in 12 months (weak signal, L14); (5) receivables +36% YoY vs revenue +12% (fuel-related, but CFO 9M-26 $313M vs $358M). What would prove us wrong: FY2026 EPS above the top of the guide (>= $7.28) with 2027 term renewals up high-single digits and power-gen revenue growth > 20% - i.e. a genuine margin step-up, not a buyback-driven EPS line. Departure from the outside view: the US seasoned-stock 5-year distribution is NOT on file (base_rates.json us_seasoned_5y), so the card's 5-year probabilities are compared with an EST naive class in the deep-dive file (P(>=3x) ~10%, P(<=0.5x) ~12% for US mid caps [EST, unverified]); our P(>=3x) is lower on purpose (a ~10%-ROTC cyclical at 17x forward needs a re-rating and a supercycle to triple). Checked by thesis:paper-call:US-KEX:* (6 calls to 2027-09-30, plus the 3 card calls).

pre_mortem: A US recession and lower refinery runs after the Middle East shock faded pushed inland utilization to the low-80s in 2027; spot rates fell 10-15%, inland margins went back to the low-teens and the P/E de-rated to 13x on lower EPS.
Data-center capex paused (financing or policy) and power-gen orders slipped; KDS margins fell back to mid-single digits while the inventory built for 2026 deliveries had to be worked down.
The Jones Act waiver was extended repeatedly and widened to inland-adjacent trades; coastal pricing broke and Washington's precedent weighed on the multiple.
Management kept buying back stock at $135-145 with revolver debt; when the cycle turned, debt/cap rose toward 35% just as earnings fell.
